English: Spindle Patch
A modest array of simple spindles and baskets, where nomadic weavers gather raw fibers and begin the first steps of textile production.
Weavers Tent
A larger, communal tent where skilled hands gather to spin, weave, and share techniques, fostering a sense of unity and shared craft.
Loom Hut
A sturdy, thatched hut sheltering several looms, enabling the production of more complex textiles and increasing the communitys output.
Dye Pavilion
A semi-permanent pavilion dedicated to dyeing fabrics, using local plants and minerals to produce vibrant cloth, attracting traders and boosting morale.
Patterned Room
A specialized enclosure where master artisans create intricate, symbolic patterns, lifting clan prestige and inspiring the people.
Textile Chamber
A fortified chamber, blending traditional craft with new techniques, producing textiles of such quality that they become treasured trade goods across the savanna.
Market Weaver Hall
A bustling hall where textiles are traded, and weavers barter with merchants from distant lands, further strengthening the clans economy and renown.
Guild Pavilion
A grand pavilion, seat of the weavers’ guild, where masters oversee training and production, ensuring the clans textile legacy will persist for generations.
Master Weavers Room
A lavish chamber reserved for the most skilled weavers, where the clans finest fabrics are woven and where traditions are codified for all to follow.
West African Weaving Guild
The pinnacle of nomadic textile mastery: a revered institution that draws artisans and traders from across the Sahel, bolstering prosperity, unity, and the clans enduring prestige.
